name: floatprefix
algorithm: Parse the longest float prefix of each of 4,096 texts "<a>.<b>e<e>;" from splitmix64 words, reps passes; each result folds bits >> 32 of the value and the bytes used (README.md).

skip.rust: no prefix parse in Rust's std: str::parse::<f64> takes a whole string, so the caller must find the float's end first, which is the task
skip.zig: no prefix parse in Zig's std: std.fmt.parseFloat takes a whole slice, so the caller must find the float's end first, which is the task
skip.go: no prefix parse in Go's std: strconv.ParseFloat takes a whole string (its prefix form, parseFloatPrefix, is unexported), so the caller must find the float's end first, which is the task
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the task has no other integer arithmetic

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the parse's correctness is std/std-text_parseprefix_test.go's (strconv.ParseFloat on the longest grammar prefix of 125,164 inputs)
